Maintenance Report — MNT-0028-001

Asset: WELL-0028 (SW-23 Well 028, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 18 Nov 2022 08:00 · Finished: 19 Nov 2022 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 30 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0028-0005 on 2022-11-17 Report written: 20 Nov 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0028-0005 at 08:00 on 2022-11-17 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.5% of the pad area, estimated 2.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 381 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 305 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0028-001 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0028-017

Asset: WELL-0028 (SW-23 Well 028, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 27 Oct 2024 08:00 · Finished: 06 Nov 2024 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 254 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0028-0103 on 2024-10-24 Report written: 07 Nov 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0028-0103 showed the wellhead at 19.6 °C with the air at 17.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 9 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0028-019

Asset: WELL-0028 (SW-23 Well 028, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 08 Dec 2024 08:00 · Finished: 01 Jan 2025 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 570 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0028-0109 on 2024-12-05 Report written: 02 Jan 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0028-0109 showed the wellhead at 14.5 °C with the air at 14.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.
